**decision: approved**

The change meets R5, R7 and R10. I found four defects, all low severity, and each is a follow-up with an owner and a review date. Under the review policy, low-severity risks can be accepted, so they don't block approval.

**What I could and couldn't run:** I ran `pose artifact-check --strict` (no errors; the only warnings are orphan claims on files outside this scope) and `pose surface-check --strict` (`findings=0`). The sandbox refused `pose validate`, `pose assess design` and the other assess and suggest tools. | Criterion | Result | Evidence and reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| assumption-integrity | passed | See below. |
| backend-concurrency | passed | `resident_git_memo.go:78-115` holds a mutex for every change to the map and the LRU list. `runtime_host.go:83-149` has a semaphore of one, and the deadline timer also covers the wait for a turn. A command that runs past its deadline is still counted by `Busy`, which feeds idle, drain and status (`runtime.go:380, 458, 484`). Proved by `resident-cache-integration` under `-race`. |
| backend-contracts | passed | `Request` is now exported, but `worktreeruntime` is an internal package. The new reply fields use `omitempty`, so slice-1 replies don't change. `pose.runtime.run/1` is new and documented. |
| backend-input-errors | finding (F2) | Inputs are bounded: 64 KiB request, 16 MiB reply, 2 MiB hosted output, 10-minute cap. `--timeout` is validated. One error path is mislabelled (F2). |
| backend-integration-impact | passed | The memo hooks into `capture` (`governance_read_view_git.go:336-380`) only when the memo is switched on. The read-view tests still pass. |
| backend-observability | passed | Refusals, deadlines and unknown outcomes carry reasons. The envelope reports `via`, `fallback_reason`, `outcome`, `epoch` and `memo_hits`. |
| compatibility | passed | Without `run` and without the memo, behaviour is unchanged. The memo is off by default, which a test checks. `status`, `stop` and `attach` keep their error types because `OutcomeUnknownError` unwraps to the original error. |
| correctness | passed | Sealed `unit:pose-mcp/go/test`. I also confirmed the six round-1/2 fixes and the round-4 fixes are in the code. |
| design-causality | passed | D1: once the earlier engine specs fixed the rest, the cost left over is Git (about 14 s of 242 `log -1` calls). Read-only Git queries tied to a fixed commit or object id don't need a freshness check, because the commit or object id is the key. |
| documentation | finding (F1, F4) | All four manuals were updated, but they contain a literal `\n\n` and leave out the 10-minute cap. |
| operability | passed | A command that never started falls back to running standalone. A command that may have run exits 1 with "may have run, not repeated, check its effects". |
| requirements | passed | Every one of R5, R7 and R10 is traced to tests in `resident-cache-integration`. |
| scope | passed | The changed files match the spec's artifact list. Only the five checks are hosted, and nothing is routed to the runtime by default. |
| security | passed | The socket is 0600 and the server checks the caller's user ID before reading. It refuses unhosted commands and a different environment digest before starting anything. Commands run as the same user, so the caller gains no authority. |
| solution-proportionality | passed (note F3) | The smallest alternative, hosting without caching, saves no time. The memo is small (115 lines) and only reaches read-only Git queries the earlier spec already identified. D1 states what would invalidate it. |

**Assumptions:**
- **Verified:**
  - Replace refs and grafts are disabled for every Git call: `--no-replace-objects` plus `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` in `git_snapshot_integrity.go:579`.
  - Linked worktrees and submodules are skipped, because `.git` must be a directory.
  - The shallow state and the repository's `.git/config` are part of the key.
  - A cache hit is admitted against the operation's budget, and is refused when it is over `limit`, the same as a fresh read.
  - Every hosted check resolves its root from the Git top-level, and none takes a path relative to the caller's directory.
- **Unresolved:** user and global Git configuration are not in the key; this is already recorded as a follow-up.
- **Accepted risks:** the environment digest is an allow-list. The speed-up figure was measured by hand, not by a test.

## Defects

- **F1 (low)** `POSE.md:949`, `locales/pt-BR/POSE.md:944`, `pose-mcp/internal/scaffold/dist/POSE.md:936`, `pose-mcp/internal/scaffold/dist/locales/pt-BR/POSE.md:944`: the new paragraph ends with a literal `\n\n` and is joined to "Review rounds", which ships to installed projects.
- **F2 (low)** `pose-mcp/internal/cli/runtime_host.go:208`: when the runtime answers with only `Error` and no `outcome` (for example, a request over 64 KiB is rejected as invalid JSON at `runtime.go:410`), the command certainly did not start. It is still reported as `unknown` and exits 1, instead of falling back to standalone as the spec requires.
- **F3 (low)** `pose-mcp/internal/pose/resident_git_memo.go:92`: the byte budget counts only key and output, not per-entry overhead, so real memory use can exceed the 256 MiB stated in D1.
- **F4 (low)** `pose-mcp/internal/worktreeruntime/runtime.go:589`: a `--timeout` above 10 minutes is silently cut to 10 minutes, and the manuals don't say so.
